Codex CXS 193 has no chocolate-specific tHg ML. FSAI 2016 attributes tHg exposure to fish (52% adults), not chocolate; no chocolate-isolated tHg value reported.

Chekri 2019 names cocoa/chocolate as contributor to Al in biscuits/desserts/pastries but reports no chocolate-isolated Al value; chocolate is bundled in mixed-meal and cereal-based food categories. FSAI 2016 reports Al by food group (cereals/bread/tea), not chocolate-specific.

Chekri 2019 mentions cocoa/chocolate as contributor to Cr in mixed infant categories but no chocolate-isolated value. FSAI 2016 attributes Cr to meat (26%) and vegetables (31%) for adults; chocolate not isolated.

Arevalo-Gardini 2017 metals list includes Cr but reports specific bean values only for Cd, Pb, Ni, Zn, Cu, Fe, Mn — no Cr concentration tabulated. Chekri 2019 names cocoa as contributor to Cr in derived foods but no cocoa-isolated value.
Chekri 2019 reports Sn values for fruit purees, formula, cereal-based foods, mixed meals — cocoa is not isolated and not flagged as Sn contributor. Codex CXS 193 sets no Sn ML for cocoa.
Both narrative reviews; neither reports fruit-specific tHg concentration values. Afonne lists Codex MLs (no tHg ML for fruits cited). Munir notes tHg toxicology but no fruit occurrence data.
Both narrative reviews discuss Cr toxicity (esp. Cr-VI) but neither reports fruit-specific Cr concentration values.

Codex CCCF17 mentions herbal botanicals only in passing for CoP scoping. Wang 2021 measures Hg and As species in mouse liver/kidney tissue after cinnabar/realgar dosing — not herbal-botanical food-matrix iAs content.

FERA UK TDS 2015 Green Vegetables group (3312 retail samples composited into food groups): Sn <0.01 mg/kg (below LOQ of ~10 µg/kg). ND-to-LOQ range encoded as [0,10] ppb. Codex CXS 193 sets no leafy-greens Sn ML.
CFS 2012 HKTDS measures iAs (not tAs) for legumes/nuts/seeds: mean 4 µg/kg iAs, n=24, 63% <LOD. Speciation rule: iAs not substitutable for tAs. Khan 2015 narrative review; no legume tAs values.

CFS 2013 HKTDS reports Al by food group (vegetables mean 4.1 mg/kg, range ND-45) but legumes not isolated as a separate group with Al value. Khan 2015 reviews bioaccumulation mechanisms without legume Al concentration values.

Afonne 2020 narrative review covers maize qualitatively (e.g., Tanzania gold mine site) but no maize-specific tAs concentration. Vasilachi 2023 mechanistic review of cereal-soil-metal interactions without grain concentration tables.
Afonne 2020 mentions Tanzania maize Hg 'above maximum tolerable limits' (Koleleni & Mbike 2018) but no specific maize tHg concentration. Vasilachi 2023 mechanistic, no values.

Masite 2022 Table 4: mopane worm (edible insect, South Africa) tAs 22.5 mg/kg = 22,500 µg/kg dry weight, single composite sample. Single_point_weak per Part 19 admission rules. Sim 2024 is methods-validation paper; mentions iAs in insect proteins at trace levels without specific tAs values for the non-soy-protein category.

Marques 2021 (Spain, retail oat drink composite): U not detected. Du 2025 is urinary-biomarker study in infants (not oat tissue). ND in derived oat beverage encoded as [0,1] ppb pending tissue-level confirmation; commodity gap remains.

Codex CXS 193 has no onion-specific iAs ML. FDA TDS FY2018-FY2020 measures total arsenic for onions (mean ~4 ppb, max 15 ppb, n=27) but does NOT speciate iAs in onions; iAs speciation rows in this dataset are limited to rice and crisped rice cereal.

Adhikari 2024 reports spring onion (Allium fistulosum, leafy) Al ~14-43 mg/kg fresh weight in Johannesburg urban-deposition setting — spring onion is a different species and edible part from mature onion bulb (Allium cepa) which is the canonical 'onions' commodity. Stasinos 2014 review mentions Al toxicity to potato roots at pH 4.5 but tabulates no Al values for onion.
Codex CXS 193 sets Pb MLs for edible offal but no iAs ML. Zhao 2024 reports offal Cd 0.03-0.5 mg/kg (n=1,406) but tabulates no iAs values for organ meats; speciation rule prohibits substituting tAs.

Scutarasu 2023 explicitly notes 'Rice bran oil: Cd and Pb values cross-referenced but specific numbers not tabulated in this section.' Silva 2025 Table A1 rice bran oil (Iran, Mohajer 2020): Pb 2.57, Cd 0.07, tAs 2.46, Ni 0.97, Zn, Cu, Mn µg/kg — Cr is NOT reported for rice bran oil specifically (olive oil has Cr 7.12-9.43; palm oil 5.36).

Pacquette 2016 is a single-laboratory ICP-MS method validation using NIST SRMs; explicitly does not report finished-product occurrence data. Thoerig 2025 systematic review summarizes per-analyte/per-matrix statistics but the source page does not break out soy-based-specific Pb values; underlying primary studies cited (Dabeka 2011, Carignan 2015, Almeida 2022, etc.) supply the sample-level data and are routed separately.
Pacquette 2016 methods validation only. Thoerig 2025 systematic review; source page does not break out soy-based-specific Cd values. Underlying primary studies route separately.
Pacquette 2016 methods validation only. Thoerig 2025 systematic review; source page does not break out soy-based-specific tHg values. Underlying primary studies route separately.

Bair 2022 narrative review identifies sweet potato among highest-risk infant-food ingredients but reports no sweet-potato iAs concentration. Houlihan 2019 HBBF reports sweet potato baby food at 19 ppb (sum of four metals, wet weight); iAs speciation was performed on 25 of 168 highest-arsenic samples only — sweet potato iAs not separately reported.

FW basis prevailing; adhikari2024 leafy DW 360-2560 ppb (anthropogenic Johannesburg); dearing2025 NZ tAs detected only in 2/153 with max 240 ppb FW; fera2015 UK TDS Green Vegetables <3 ppb FW; romero-crespo2023 lettuce 12,500 ppb FW mining-affected (excluded from typical range); saleem2025 vegetables tAs range 9-436 ppb DW; wang2023 cabbage/cauliflower/spinach context. Typical excludes mining hotspots; p95 reflects high-bound non-mining detections.

Most measurements below LOD: dearing2025 all 153 samples <10 ppb FW; fera2015 Green Vegetables <5 ppb FW. saleem2025 spinach max 11.3 ppb DW. adhikari2024 leafy mean range 120-2450 ppb DW (anthropogenic deposition outlier). codex-cxs-193-1995 and tan2022 carry no concentration values for this cell.

codex regulatory only; fera2015 reports iAs in Green Vegetables <12 ppb (LOQ) — below LOD; sadee2023 is a methodology review without leafy-green-specific iAs distribution. Only one source provides a censored upper-bound; insufficient quantitative basis to synthesize a range.

fera2015 UK TDS Green Vegetables Al 1.28 mg/kg FW (1280 ppb FW). adhikari2024 leafy veg combined Al mean range 318-1414 mg/kg DW (Johannesburg anthropogenic). wang2023 Ningxia veg Al context only. Wide range reflects DW vs FW basis split and anthropogenic vs typical.

dai2024 meat (n=807) mean tAs 7.9-10.8 ppb wet weight, P95 15.2 ppb wet weight. fera2015 UK TDS Carcass Meat tAs <6 ppb FW (LOQ); meli2024 only reports detection rates, no concentrations; wysok2025 sheep casings tAs 36±29 ppb wet weight (offal-adjacent matrix). cfs2012 reports iAs not tAs; fda-tds-elements-2018-2020 source page has no extracted per-food values; fsai2016 contribution context only; liang2019 cereal-only data; wang2023 meat Cr only.

albishi2026 cassava flour controls tAs 10-11 ppb DW (n=3 per treatment). clair-caliot2021 carrot at 500 µg/L As irrigation 3,500 ppb DW (high-As experimental); not typical baseline. romero-crespo2023 carrots 1,940 ppb FW, turnips 2,550 ppb FW (mining-affected). Typical range reflects baseline; p95 captures mining/spiked-irrigation context. dearing2025 root-veg subset mostly ND; khan2015 review; malone2024 soil only; sadee2023 review; saleem2025 root subset not specifically broken out for tAs.

hopfner2025 powdered cow-milk-based infant formula iAs BfR MEAL mean 4.55 ppb DW (50% <LOQ); German food monitoring mean 20 ppb (all at LOQ). The other five sources (ashley-martin2022, chen2025, codex-cxs-193-1995, fda-tds-elements-2018-2020, fera2015) provide biomonitoring/exposure/regulatory context but no dairy-specific iAs concentrations on their source pages. Range reflects formula matrix; raw cow milk iAs occurrence not directly available.

All four sources address breastmilk iAs in narrative/exposure context (formula-fed infants have higher urinary iAs biomarkers than breastfed). None report a quantitative breastmilk iAs concentration on the source page. Carignan papers report cohort outcomes; Pikounis reports biomarkers; Thoerig 2025 is a systematic review without quoted breastmilk iAs values.

hands2024 US dark chocolate tAs n=55: mean 94 ppb, median 50 ppb, min 17 ppb, max 200 ppb. hands2024-multiyear is companion paper with same 72-product dataset across 2014-2022. chekri2019 French infant TDS does not include chocolate matrix; fsai2016 carries no chocolate-specific tAs values.

codex-cccf17-2024 addresses Cd MLs only. codex-cxs-193-1995 sets cocoa Cd MLs but no cocoa iAs maximum levels. mancuso2024 cardiovascular review names cocoa as Cd source; no iAs concentration. zhao2024 review reports cocoa/tea/coffee Cd 0.0001-1.8 mg/kg but no iAs-specific cocoa value. None of the four sources quantitatively report iAs in cocoa.

adhikari2024 Johannesburg leafy veg combined Ni mean range 8-198.7 mg/kg DW (8,000-198,710 ppb DW); includes mint and coriander as herbal botanicals. rossini-oliva2024 reports no Ni-specific value for herbal botanicals on source page. salmani2023 herbal teas review does not extract Ni values. zafeiraki2021 measured Ni in hemp but no concentrations extracted in source-page summary. Single-source synthesis; wide range reflects market-type variation.

milani2023 Brazilian retail soy beverages tAs <38.2 µg/L (LOQ) across isolate-protein, hydrosoluble-extract, soybean. collado-lopez2025 without-stage soy formula As median 52 ppb. wang2023 beans Pb/Cr but no tAs reported; zhang2026 soybean grain THQ<1 specific As value not extracted. Range reflects beverage/formula matrices (not bare soybean); HMI architecture treats soy ingredient as supplied to plant-milk and formula products.

chekri2019 French infant TDS does not include chocolate among its tabulated infant categories. codex-cxs-193-1995 is regulatory limits only. fsai2016 reports tin <4% of JECFA PTWI across diet with no chocolate-specific value. No quantitative chocolate Sn concentration available.

cicero2022 cinnamon (Indonesia) Ni 2.766 mg/kg DW (n=1). lhaac2025 spice powders Ni majority <2 mg/kg DW; cinnamon not separately broken out. tinggi2025 spices/herbs overall Ni mean 1.11 mg/kg (n=69); black pepper highest at 2.08 mg/kg; cinnamon-specific Ni not extracted on source page but falls within overall range. Range reflects 1-3 mg/kg DW typical, with upper bound for context.
aisyiah2025 Taiwan colostrum Al 56.45±22.77 ng/mL (~56 µg/L). atsdr-2008 breast milk Al 9.2-49 µg/L. katrynska2026 confirms detection but no specific values. Range covers both sources.

du2025 is urinary biomarker comparison study (not oatmeal Hg content). marques2021 reports Hg ND in oat drink. rubio2023 reports Hg in rice (1.3 ppb DW) and wheat (1 ppb DW) only — no oat-specific Hg concentration on source page. No quantitative oat tHg value available.

marcelino2026 liver As <LOQ (0.4 mg/kg DW) in >50% of cattle samples. meligy2024 camel offal As reported as low-level trace; specific values not extracted on source page. zhao2024 review summarizes Cd in offal but does not provide As-specific organ-meat distribution. No usable quantitative tAs value for organ meats.

collado-lopez2025 reports Hg detection rates in formula by protein source but no soy-specific tHg median on source page. ibrahim2024 is household food Hg (Hadejia Nigeria); not soy-specific. marques2021 reports Hg not detected in soy drink. No quantitative soy tHg concentration.

milani2023 soy beverages Cr 1.8 µg/L isolate-protein (range <10.9-11.0); hydrosoluble-extract and soybean beverages <10.9 µg/L (LOQ). wang2023 beans Cr mean 753.6 ppb, max 2280.8 ppb DW. zhang2026 soybean kernel Cr THQ<1, specific value not extracted on source page. Range reflects beverage matrix (low) and bean matrix (higher) and DW vs FW basis difference. Total chromium (not Cr-VI).

muniz2018 tomato sauce Sn metallic can mean 125-258 ppb wet weight (n=7); plastic 20-51; cellulosic 55-80; glass 57-59. shavali-gilani2025 canned tomato paste Sn 410 ppb wet weight. kangre2024 Ghana canned tomato Sn 'consistent' across display conditions (specific value not extracted but within range). Tin migration from tinplate cans is the primary driver; range reflects packaging-type variation.

brzezinska-rojek2023 beetroot supplements Pb <LOQ (0.035 mg/kg DW = <35 ppb) in all 37 samples. katebe2024 Beta vulgaris leaves Pb 8-29 ppb DW across treatments D0-D4 in Kashamata garden (some D3/D4 ND). Single-experiment basis; typical reflects observed range.

katebe2024 Beta vulgaris (beet) leaves Cd range ND-15 ppb DW across D0-D4 treatments in Kashamata garden. brzezinska-rojek2023 reports beetroot-supplement Cd as per-daily-dose (3-78 µg/d.d.), not directly comparable to ppb in raw beet; not used as concentration source. Single-source synthesis from pot experiment.

bair2022 names carrots among highest-risk infant ingredients but reports no carrot-specific iAs concentration. houlihan2019 HBBF reports carrot baby food average 28 ppb sum of four metals; iAs speciation was performed on only 25 of 168 highest-As foods (rice-dominant) — carrot-specific iAs not separately reported. No quantitative carrot iAs concentration.

codex-cxs-193-1995 is regulatory standard — no chocolate iAs measurement. fsai2016 Irish TDS does not report a chocolate-specific iAs value (chocolate aggregated within snacks/confectionery; iAs contributors dominated by cereals 81% adult, 94% child). No quantitative chocolate iAs available.

Codex CXS 193-1995 milk Pb ML is 20 ug/kg.

Below-LOQ FDA TDS US non-detects (RL 1 ug/kg) treated as left-censored, not zero. Cd in commercial milk is consistently at or below ~1-2 ug/kg (starska2011 Poland 1, chen2020 China 0.77, davidov2019 Serbia 10); ibrahim2024 Egyptian raw milk mean 90 ug/kg is a contaminated-market tail (46% of that survey exceeded the Egyptian Pb limit) and is not adopted as the central value.

Total mercury in milk is genuinely trace and below the analytical reporting limit in most datasets: pankiewicz2012 Polish milk 0.03-0.06 ug/kg, starska2011 milk 1 ug/kg, marques2021 Spain <LD, FDA TDS <1 ug/kg (RL). The published value is the left-censored upper bound, not a measured zero.

FDA TDS US non-detect (RL 20 ug/kg) treated as left-censored, not zero. davidov2019 Serbia reports mean Ni 119 ug/kg in cow milk (ICP-OES, DL 5 ug/kg); marques2021 detected Ni in 6/32 milk/drink samples. Ni in milk is feed- and environment-driven and spans below-RL to ~120 ug/kg.

FDA TDS US non-detect (RL 25 ug/kg) treated as left-censored, not zero. davidov2019 Serbia reports total Cr 18 ug/kg in cow milk, below the FDA RL. Both datasets place milk Cr at or below ~20-25 ug/kg; the value is the left-censored upper bound.

FDA TDS US cheddar non-detect (RL 4 ug/kg) treated as left-censored. Cheese-making concentrates milk metals ~6-10x, and European/Egyptian matured-cheese datasets report Pb far above the US cheddar RL: capcarova2023 Italian mozzarella 580-810, ibrahim2024 Egyptian Ras 610/Domiati 550/Karish 340, erol2025 an artisanal Golot outlier at 1788 ug/kg. Wide range and low confidence reflect an unresolved US-vs-ex-US discrepancy; direction is toward the literature (not a measured zero).

FDA TDS US cheddar non-detect (RL 1 ug/kg) treated as left-censored. ibrahim2024 Egyptian cheese Cd 120-250 ug/kg (Ras 250, Domiati 180, Karish 120); starska2011 milk-products ~2. Range spans US non-detect to Egyptian matured cheese; not a measured zero.

Total mercury in cheese is trace and below the reporting limit in most samples (FDA TDS <1 RL; pankiewicz2012 cream/cottage cheese 0.05-0.23 ug/kg); erol2025 reports one artisanal Telli outlier at 468 ug/kg, treated as an extreme not a central value. The value is the left-censored upper bound.

FDA TDS US cheddar non-detect (RL 40 ug/kg) treated as left-censored. capcarova2023 Italian mozzarella reports Ni 720-1610 ug/kg in solid fractions (feed- and processing-driven). Range spans US non-detect to European mozzarella; not a measured zero.

FDA TDS US cheddar non-detect (RL 50 ug/kg) treated as left-censored, not zero. No cheddar-specific total-Cr detect is available in the focused set; the value is the left-censored upper bound at the FDA reporting limit.
